source: cortex's status record, maintained in the repository and checked against main and its planning store

items.label: Operators trigger schema emergence
items.detail: cortex schema: proposals applied or recorded.

items.label: Operators measure how well facts are supported
items.detail: cortex quality: a judged sample and a pass rate.

items.label: Structured imports end what a source dropped
items.detail: Files input and dropped: Supersede.

items.label: A changed value supersedes the old one
items.detail: replaces: true through EKR 0.0.31.

items.label: Facts are dated by when their source said it
items.detail: Evidence time from the document; EKR 0.0.31.

items.label: File records map ids to names through a lookup file
items.detail: lookup and fallback_text on records specs.

items.label: The test suite is free of the Text file busy race
items.detail: 20 of 20 full runs under load exit 0.

items.label: An existing store becomes an instance without reseeding
items.detail: cortex adopt copies a SQLite store with its -wal or uses a PostgreSQL store in place; --host and --seen carry its identity and seen state.

items.label: A bad run can be undone from the snapshot taken before it
items.detail: cortex restore puts back the store and state/ and snapshots the current state first.

items.label: Scheduled runs verified with nobody at the keyboard
items.detail: 15 runs of a real systemd user timer in 15 minutes, all exit 0; the 24 h window on a real instance comes with the first web instance.

items.label: Names and links stay out of the model; a gate refuses what survives
items.detail: Url, known_names and RareName placeholders are restored before storage; refuse_if_left checks what the model would see.

items.label: Structured sources import records with no model call
items.detail: Fields map to nodes, aliases, properties and relations; identity is adapter:operation:id.

items.label: An instance from one spec file
items.detail: cortex create reads a cortex.instance/1 file, seeds one EKR store (SQLite, or PostgreSQL as the spec names), applies the seed schema, adds the sources and installs a timer per source and a viewer.

items.label: Updating sources, model and serve settings
items.detail: cortex update replaces the frozen spec and adds new sources; a changed seed is refused (seed-change-refused).

items.label: A store on SQLite or PostgreSQL, per instance
items.detail: store: {backend: postgres, value: {config}} names an ekr.postgres/1 file; with a connection, ekr starts through connectors connections launch and reads the password from descriptor 3 as its password_file (EKR 0.0.32), so no file cortex writes holds it.

items.label: Removing an instance keeps its data
items.detail: cortex remove stops and deletes the timers and the viewer; the instance directory and its store stay.

items.label: Web sources: search, or listed sites read as pages or crawled
items.detail: Through any Connectors adapter that answers datasource.websearch/v1alpha1; tavily when the spec names none.

items.label: Connectors sources: records of any admitted operation
items.detail: One invocation per input; records, id, time and text are read from the answer by dotted paths and templates.

items.label: Files sources: local files matching a glob
Connectors sources walk pages, children and a time window
items.detail: Token, PageNumber and Keyset paging; a child operation per parent; {since} and {until} in the inputs open at the last successful run with a 5-minute overlap.

items.label: Only new or changed documents are extracted
items.detail: A document is new when its key was never applied and changed when its text hash differs; a changed one waits until its last fetch is older than refresh_after_days.

items.label: Extraction by an isolated model call
items.detail: claude -p with no tools, no settings sources and no MCP servers, answering in the JSON form of EKR's extraction document; cortex mints every evidence item and refuses facts citing any other.

items.label: Credential-shaped text is masked before storage
items.detail: Private keys, common token shapes and secret assignments. Personal data a redaction policy names is replaced by placeholders in the prompt and restored before storage.

items.label: Two failed runs in a row disable a source
items.detail: Timers run with --record-failure; cortex source enable switches the source back on.

items.label: Viewer and MCP line per instance
items.detail: A systemd user service runs ekr view on 127.0.0.1; cortex mcp-line prints the claude mcp add line that serves the store through ekr mcp.

items.label: Specified in ESS, model generated, 34 conformance scenarios
items.detail: spec/ generates the model and the spec file's serde types; tests/conformance.rs runs every scenario of spec/suite.json.

items.label: Facts from a web page cite the page as URL evidence
items.detail: Waits on an EKR release that admits URL evidence; until then a page is cited as a HumanStatement naming its URL.

items.label: Extraction produces edges between the nodes it finds
What a source has seen is part of the specification
items.detail: The specification declares the record, SeenDocument, owned by Source; the run that writes it stays an UNMAPPED rule, held by the Rust tests, until ESS can state an effect on many records.

items.label: CI runs task check on every pull request
